1502.author: yuanzhou75
1502.body:
## What happens

Four rules in `apps/desktop/src/styles/design.css` draw secondary text at `#808080`, `#8c8c8c` and `#a6a6a6`. All of it is normal-size text — 11 px, 12 px, 12.5 px — so WCAG 2.1 AA applies at **4.5:1** (SC 1.4.3; the large-text exemption starts at 18 pt, or 14 pt bold). Measured against the surfaces they actually render on, every one is below the floor, and two of them are below 3:1:

| rule | colour | size | surface it is drawn on | contrast |
| --- | --- | --- | --- | --- |
| `.settings-field-hint` | `#808080` | 12.5 px | `#fff` — the settings panel (`.config-panel` and `.config-backdrop` are `#fff`; `.settings-main` is `#fff`) | **3.95:1** |
| the same rule inside `.settings-ability-option.is-selected` | `#808080` | 12.5 px | `#f4f8ff` (`--primary-softer`) | **3.71:1** |
| `.session-flyout-desc` | `#8c8c8c` | 12 px | `#fff` — `.session-menu-flyout` is `#fff` | **3.36:1** |
| the same rule while its row is hovered | `#8c8c8c` | 12 px | `#f5f5f5` — `.session-flyout-row:hover` | **3.08:1** |
| `.session-flyout-note` (added for #1330, same colour) | `#8c8c8c` | 12 px | `#fff` | **3.36:1** |
| `.expert-note` | `#8c8c8c` | 12 px | `#fff` — the 专家 flyout | **3.36:1** |
| `.doc-tab-hint` | `#a6a6a6` | 11 px | `#f0f0f0` (`--surface-sunk`, the workspace panel) or `#fff` inside a `.workspace-section` | **2.14:1 / 2.43:1** |

Ratios are WCAG 2.1 relative luminance against the background named in the same row.

The two darkest cases are worth naming on their own: `#a6a6a6` on `#f0f0f0` is **2.14:1**, and `#8c8c8c` on the hover row is **3.08:1** — the second one only appears while the pointer is over the row the reader is reading, which is exactly when they need it.

## These are user-visible text, not decoration

- `.settings-field-hint` carries the sentence under a settings field: the skill-name rule (`TEXT.settings.skills.nameHint`, and `nameInvalid` in the same element), the specialist instructions hint and the capability hint (`TEXT.settings.system.specialists.instructionsHint`, `capabilitiesHint`) — `views/settings/SkillForm.tsx`, `views/settings/system/SpecialistForm.tsx`. Only the `is-error` variant switches to `--danger`, and that one is not part of this report.
- `.expert-note` carries the flyout's own status: `TEXT.composer.expertsLoading` (“正在读取专家…”) and `TEXT.composer.expertsEmpty` (“没有匹配的专家。”) — `views/Composer.tsx`.
- `.session-flyout-desc` carries the line that explains what each choice does, under the label of every row of 审查档位, 请求批准 and 会话设置.
- `.doc-tab-hint` carries the folder that tells two same-named documents apart in the tab strip — `views/WorkspacePanel.tsx`.

None of them is an icon, a placeholder, a disabled control or decorative text, so none of them is exempt.

## Where it comes from

`apps/desktop/src/styles/design.css` at `main` `d9f5a3da`:

- `:2208` `.session-flyout-desc { color: #8c8c8c; font-size: 12px; … }`
- `:2216` `.session-flyout-note { color: #8c8c8c; font-size: 12px; … }`
- `:2442` `.expert-note { color: #8c8c8c; font-size: 12px; … }`
- `:2993` `.doc-tab-hint { color: #a6a6a6; font-size: 11px; … }`
- `:4225` `.settings-field-hint { color: #808080; font-size: 12.5px; … }`

Two of the three colours are already tokens, so the fix is at token level rather than per selector: `apps/desktop/src/styles/tokens.css:36` `--text-faint: #8c8c8c`, `:35` `--muted-light: #a6a6a6`; `#808080` is written literally. The surfaces in the table are `--surface: #ffffff` (`:20`), `--surface-sunk: #f0f0f0` (`:24`), `--surface-hover: #ededed` (`:23`), `--primary-softer: #f4f8ff` (`:41`), and `.session-flyout-row:hover { background: #f5f5f5 }` (`:2177`).

## Suggested fix

Move all three to one secondary-text value that clears 4.5:1 on the worst surface in the table:

| candidate | on `#fff` | on `#f5f5f5` | on `#f0f0f0` | on `#f4f8ff` | on `#ededed` |
| --- | --- | --- | --- | --- | --- |
| `#666666` | 5.74 | 5.27 | 5.04 | 5.39 | 4.90 |
| `#777777` (today's `--muted`) | 4.48 | 4.11 | 3.93 | 4.20 | 3.83 |

`#666666` is the value already agreed for the desktop sidebar hints in #1486, which is the same defect on a different surface; using it here as well keeps one secondary colour across the desktop instead of a third shade. Note that `--muted` (`#777777`) does **not** clear the floor on the darker surfaces, so it cannot simply be reused.

## Related

#1486 reports the same problem for the sidebar and the landing surface. This report is the settings, flyout and document-tab half of it; the two do not overlap.

## Environment

- Windows 11, desktop renderer (React in Chromium), zh-CN and en.
- Colour values, surfaces and sizes read from `apps/desktop/src/styles` at `main` `d9f5a3da8c281829d6791efbbe3ce9392bf936b6`; ratios computed with the WCAG 2.1 relative-luminance formula.
- No backend, no data and no behaviour involved: this is a stylesheet and token change.
1502.title: [Bug]: Desktop settings, flyout and document-tab hint text misses WCAG AA (2.14:1 – 3.95:1)

1506.author: agent-ci-infra-bot[bot]
1506.body:
### Checklist

- [x] I searched existing Issues and PRs for `UNEXPECTED_SWARM_CHECKS`; nothing tracks this failure (the only hit is merged PR #1361, which introduced the check).
- [x] I reproduced the reconciliation failure locally at `e63099ab` with synthetic mocked artifacts; no E2E stack was started.
- [x] This reports a CI reconciliation regression, not a product failure: all 195 planned mocked cases passed in this run.

### 🐞 Detailed Description of the Problem

[Dispatch Nightly #113](https://github.com/openJiuwen-ai/sciencediscovery/actions/runs/46030598150) (attempt 1, `main @ e63099ab3b0b2bb30e9ecea432ee6be69efcc8a1`, `profile=daily`, `backend=jiuwenswarm`, `CI_E2E_LOCAL_CONCURRENCY=2`) failed **only** in `Gate / merge-gate` (job `140705976460`), step `Reconcile mocked results`:

```
##[group]Run node .ci/mocked-report.mjs .ci-mocked-plan/plan.json .ci-mocked-results .ci-results
### Mocked E2E: FAIL

Planned 195; executed 195; passed 195.

- standard-config: UNEXPECTED_SWARM_CHECKS

##[error]Process completed with exit code 1.
```

The mocked layer that produced those artifacts was green: `Gate / L2 E2E (mocked, standard-config)` (job `140613911090`) concluded **success** with `| e2e | 58a08ac09c38 | 75 | 75 | 75 | 75 | 1 | 0 | 0 | 0 | 0 | 0 |` (75/75 passed, 1 passed after retry), and the other four mocked shards were green too. `Report the outcome` (job `140706111813`) then failed with `RESULT: failure` for the same reason. So the failure is purely in result reconciliation.

#### Root cause

1. `test/support/tagged/retry.mjs:14` enables the per-case retry only for the `daily` and `release` profiles, so this run retried one failed journey:

   ```
   Repeating 1 failed case(s): playwright:test/issue-143-proxy-settings.spec.ts::mocked/issue-143-proxy-settings.spec.ts/issue-143-proxy-settings.spec/custom%20URL%20remains%20complete%20after%20refresh%20and%20is%20prefilled%20for%20editing
   ```

2. `test/support/tagged/shared.mjs:487-491` names the retry result directory `<batchKey>-retry`, i.e. `mocked-standard-config-global-retry`, and passes it as the retry's `CI_RESULTS_DIR`. `test/support/tagged/retry-runner.mjs:183` uses it for the isolated `.ci/run-e2e.sh` child (the job log shows the retry worktree `.ci-retry/mocked-standard-config-global-retry`).

3. `test/support/tagged/retry-runner.mjs:25-31` (`batchLaunchConfig`) reuses the failed case's batch launch config, including `checks: 'run'` when that batch carries the 9 JiuwenSwarm checks (`test/support/tagged/execution.mjs:177,199` keeps them exclusively on `mocked-standard-config-global`). The retry therefore re-ran the supplemental checks on the retry stack — the job log shows all nine (`history`, `history-names`, `run-shell`, `host-tools`, `approvals`, `skills`, `skill-switch`, `trajectory`, `language`) a second time at `16:22:52Z`-`16:23:25Z`.

4. `.ci/run-e2e.sh:448` writes that evidence to `$CI_RESULTS_DIR/e2e/jiuwenswarm-checks.json`, so the retry produced `mocked-standard-config-global-retry/e2e/jiuwenswarm-checks.json` inside `.ci-results`, which `.github/workflows/ci.yml:688-696` uploads wholesale as the `mocked-e2e-results-standard-config` artifact.

5. `.ci/mocked-report.mjs:36-39` (added by the merged PR #1361, commit `92f40dab9`) audits **every** `mocked-*` sub-directory of a shard artifact and fails with `UNEXPECTED_SWARM_CHECKS` for any of them other than the single designated check batch that contains `e2e/jiuwenswarm-checks.json`. The retry directory is not one of the plan's batches (`mockedBatches()` derives only `-fresh`/`-global`), so the legitimate retry evidence is classified as out-of-bounds.

In short: the audit behaves as written, but the retry path now produces evidence that no accounting consumes and that the audit necessarily rejects. Both halves predate the failure individually; they were only combined when the audit was widened in #1361.

#### Trigger conditions and impact

- Only `daily` (Nightly) and `release` runs can hit it, because only they retry failed cases (`retry.mjs:14`). `pr` and `merge_group` (`merge`) runs never create a `*-retry` directory, so PR CI and the merge queue are unaffected.
- Within a run, it needs a first-attempt failure in the **`mocked-standard-config-global`** batch, i.e. the lane that carries the nine supplemental checks. A retry of `-fresh`, `-global-2`, `standard-journeys`, `research`, `governed` or `literature` runs with `CI_E2E_SWARM_CHECKS=off` and leaves no checks file, so it does not trip the audit today.
- Consequence: a green mocked layer (195/195, as here) is reported as `UNEXPECTED_SWARM_CHECKS`, the whole Nightly/Release gate is red, and the release evidence shows a mocked failure that did not happen.
- Secondary cost of the same defect: the retry re-runs nine live JiuwenSwarm checks (about 45 s of extra stack work), and any spurious check failure on that second stack turns into `PROVIDER_FAULT_RETRY_FAILED`, a flakiness source unrelated to the one case being retried.

### Verification performed

- Read the failing job log (`Reconcile mocked results`, `Report the outcome`), the green mocked job log (`Repeating 1 failed case(s)` at `16:20:52Z`, the retry worktree, and the second run of the nine checks), and the code paths cited above at `e63099ab`.
- Reproduced with the real code: built a `daily` plan plus worker artifacts via `createPlan`/`verifyResults` and ran `reconcileMocked()` from `.ci/mocked-report.mjs`.
  - Without the retry directory: `PASS 0 []`.
  - After adding only `mocked-e2e-results-standard-config/mocked-standard-config-global-retry/e2e/jiuwenswarm-checks.json`: `FAIL 1 ["standard-config: UNEXPECTED_SWARM_CHECKS"]` with `planned 5; executed 5; passed 5` — the same shape as the reported `Planned 195; executed 195; passed 195.`
  - Running the same reproduction against `.ci/mocked-report.mjs` at `92f40dab9^` (before PR #1361) returns `PASS` in both cases, which pins the regression.
- The first-attempt failure that triggered the retry (`test/issue-143-proxy-settings.spec.ts:277`, `toBeVisible()` on the prefilled proxy URL) passed on retry and is not part of this issue; it is ordinary product/journey flakiness absorbed by the retry policy.

### Suggested bounded fix

Make the isolated retry re-run only what it retries — the failed case — and never the exactly-once supplemental checks:

- In `test/support/tagged/retry-runner.mjs`, have `isolatedRetryConfig()` (or `batchLaunchConfig(..., { retry: true })`) emit `checks: 'off'` regardless of `batch.checks`, so `batchLaunchEnvironment()` sets `CI_E2E_SWARM_CHECKS=off` for a retry. The retry verdict already comes from its own Playwright report (`SCIENCE_TAG_PW_REPORT`), and the first attempt's checks evidence stays authoritative.
- Keep `.ci/mocked-report.mjs` strict. Do **not** simply whitelist `*-retry` there: that would silence a real duplicate-checks run instead of preventing it. If a defensive allowance is still wanted, accept a retry directory only when it holds no `e2e/jiuwenswarm-checks.json`, and keep every other `mocked-*` directory failing with `UNEXPECTED_SWARM_CHECKS`.

Suggested regression tests (both fail before the fix, pass after):

- `test/support/tagged/tests/retry-environment.test.mjs`: `batchLaunchEnvironment(isolatedRetryConfig({ ..., batch: { group: 'mocked', fixture: 'standard', checks: swarmChecks } }).launchConfig).CI_E2E_SWARM_CHECKS === 'off'`. Today only batches with `checks: []` are covered; a checks-carrying batch returns `'run'`.
- `.ci/mocked-shards.test.mjs` or `.ci/self-hosted-merge-queue.test.mjs`: a shard artifact containing a `mocked-standard-config-global-retry` directory without checks evidence still reconciles `PASS`, while a `jiuwenswarm-checks.json` in any other `mocked-*` directory still yields `UNEXPECTED_SWARM_CHECKS` (so the audit's intent is preserved).

### Detailed Environment Information Description

- GitHub-hosted `ubuntu-26.04` runner, Actions runner `2.338.2`, workflow `.github/workflows/nightly.yml` (Nightly #113) calling `ci.yml` via `workflow_call`.
- Inputs: `profile=daily`, `backend=jiuwenswarm` (repository variable default), `max-parallel=2`; matrix shard `standard-config` with `CI_E2E_LOCAL_CONCURRENCY=2`.
- The failing step ran `node .ci/mocked-report.mjs .ci-mocked-plan/plan.json .ci-mocked-results .ci-results` at `19:40:01Z`.

### Version Information

- Repository: `openJiuwen-ai/sciencediscovery`, `main @ e63099ab3b0b2bb30e9ecea432ee6be69efcc8a1` (run head and tested SHA).
- Regression introduced by `92f40dab9b1a1cf65a6716ced5459afc321f38a0` ("ci: run standard mocked E2E shards across 2 isolated local stacks", merged as PR #1361), which added the `mocked-*` directory audit in `.ci/mocked-report.mjs`; the retry directory and its `checks: 'run'` launch config existed before it (`bdc81300b`, "fix: isolate tagged case retries").
- Nightly #111 (`dfdcc9eb`, 2026-11-26) is the last dispatch run in the same series that stayed green, and it had no retried mocked case.

1506.title: [Bug]: Nightly merge-gate fails with UNEXPECTED_SWARM_CHECKS when a mocked case is retried

1509.author: HongyeZhou
1509.body:
## User outcome

A reader of a literature report can tell what was searched, what could not be searched, how evidence was selected, and why the report uses its output language.

This consolidates the unfinished scope of #416 and #419. Their original reports, artifacts and screenshots remain the historical evidence. This is an administrative consolidation, not a claim that either feature has been delivered.

## Scope and acceptance

- [ ] Saved literature reports include a concise Methods/Search section naming sources actually used, fallback sources, search date, queries and applicable date/language filters.
- [ ] Record retrieved/screened/included counts when measured. Otherwise state "not computed"; never invent counts or imply a systematic review for a brief scan.
- [ ] Disclose source failures and resulting coverage limitations. A provider failure must not silently narrow the evidence while the report claims broader coverage.
- [ ] State the preprint, grey-literature and non-English inclusion policy, or explicitly mark these categories out of scope. Do not require every brief scan to search every category.
- [ ] Define and document report-language behavior for explicit language requests, English/Chinese UI locales and no explicit output-language request. An English report answering an English prompt is not itself a defect. Provide a locale-aware summary if that is the selected policy.
- [ ] Validate saved artifacts as well as the visible report using the original brief CRISPR/SCD scan and deterministic provider fixtures covering fallback, provider failure and unavailable counts. Verify explicit language requests and both UI locales; report real-provider verification separately from mocked coverage.

## Boundaries

Claim excerpts, citation fidelity, unverifiable evidence states and Quick/Deep review coverage remain in #669. A mandatory standard-of-care comparison table is not part of this issue; that optional template proposal is recorded in #417. Keep disclosure proportional to a brief scan and avoid turning it into a mandatory systematic review.
1509.title: [Feature] Disclose literature search methods, coverage and report-language policy

1510.author: HongyeZhou
1510.body:
## Purpose

Track the remaining first-use validation and onboarding materials from #22 as a finite delivery task. Closing the original umbrella is administrative, not proof that its entire acceptance passed.

## Existing work and ownership

- One-click sample data, automatic Project/Session creation and the prefilled analysis prompt remain in #566.
- Model registration entry points and save semantics remain in #692.
- Use those issues for implementation rather than duplicating their scope here. File concrete setup/recovery defects found during validation separately and link them below.

## Acceptance

- [ ] Define one supported released-version journey: obtain/open the app, connect a model, upload the supplied licensed CSV, produce a useful chart, request a refinement, save/export and reopen the work. Name the release, supported computer types and sample-data licence.
- [ ] Verify that journey in English and Chinese, including discoverable start actions, language switching, minimum model setup with a connection test, early compatibility feedback, and errors that preserve user input and provide a recovery action. Record actual outcomes and link remaining blockers; do not claim untested platforms pass.
- [ ] Publish and link a 5-7 minute first-result walkthrough from the project entry page, with sample file, prompt, transcript, English/Chinese captions, prerequisites and accelerated waits labelled.
- [ ] Publish and link the 6-8 minute comparison requested in #22: the same IMO 2026 Day 2 Problem 5 task with the same model and comparable budgets, direct conversation versus ScienceDiscovery. Verify the problem/reference and proofs before publishing; report the observed outcome, actual time and cost, including ties or failures. Preserve the original reference links and full solution-family requirement from #22.
- [ ] Observe ten unfamiliar users attempting the sample journey, including users who have not watched the videos. Report unaided completion and friction points; eight of ten is the proposed target, not an existing result. Fix or separately track blocking friction and record next-week return observations when available.
- [ ] Verify the entry page exposes a working help/feedback route and the current GitHub contribution route. Provide a short first-contribution guide, bounded starter tasks with named reviewers, and checks runnable without paid models or special hardware; explain how remaining validation is supported.
- [ ] Publish a final result with release/SHA, journey evidence, materials links, user observations and the disposition of every linked blocker. Assign owners when delivery is scheduled; no owner or deadline is implied by this cleanup.

## Historical context

#22 preserves the original trial feedback and broader product goals. Its old GitCode contribution-routing statement must not be copied as current guidance. Existing delivered UI behavior is a baseline to verify, not a request to reimplement it. New paid runs, user recruitment and publication are future delivery work, not actions performed by this triage.
1510.title: [Tracking] Validate the released first-use journey and publish onboarding materials

1511.author: agent-ci-infra-bot[bot]
1511.body:
### Checklist

- [x] I have searched for related issues but did not get the expected help.
- [x] This bug has not been fixed in the latest version.
- [x] Please note that if your bug description lacks corresponding environment information and a minimal reproducible demo, it will be difficult for us to reproduce and resolve the issue, which will reduce the possibility of receiving feedback, or even lead to the issue being closed.

### 🐞 Detailed Description of the Problem

**What happens.** Nightly run [46080401663](https://github.com/openJiuwen-ai/sciencediscovery/actions/runs/46080401663) (`main` @ `a70ef94`, `workflow_dispatch`, `profile: daily`, backend `jiuwenswarm`) fails on exactly one real case: shard `research-8`, PUCT-COMPRESS. The in-job isolated retry repeats it on a second, fresh stack and fails the same way.

**Evidence** (job [140778085432](https://github.com/openJiuwen-ai/sciencediscovery/actions/runs/46080401663/job/140778085432)):

```text
attempt 1        01:18:42  ✘ test/evolve-compression-real.spec.ts:43  (19.3m)
  Error: Search result code must be persisted as an artifact
  expect(received).toBeTruthy()  Received: undefined
  - Timeout 30000ms exceeded while waiting on the predicate
  > 172 | }, { timeout: 30_000, message: "Search result code must be persisted as an artifact" }).toBeTruthy();
        at test/evolve-compression-real.spec.ts:172:93

isolated retry   01:39:08  ✘ test/evolve-compression-real.spec.ts:43  (18.6m)
  same error, same line, run in .ci-retry/real-standard-retry (fresh worktree at a70ef94)
```

Shard accounting (`real-e2e/tagged/summary.json`, printed in the same job):

```text
| e2e-real | `a37b5e87e214` | 1 | 1 | 1 | 0 | 0 | 1 | 0 | 0 | 0 | 0 |
{"status":"FAIL",...,"passed":0,"failed":1,"provider_fault":0}
- e2e-real: PROVIDER_FAULT_RETRY_FAILED: 1
- e2e-real: PLAYWRIGHT_WORKER_FAILED: 1
```

Both problem codes are the retry's own exit classification, not a provider outage: `PROVIDER_FAULT_RETRY_FAILED` is `retryFailed(code)` from `test/support/tagged/retry.mjs` ("the retry process itself failed before producing a usable final result", here exit 1 after the case failed again), `PLAYWRIGHT_WORKER_FAILED` is the first batch exiting non-zero without a recovered case (`test/support/tagged/shared.mjs:554`), and `provider_fault: 0` means the provider-fault detector (`test/support/tagged/provider-fault.mjs`) found no gateway status or transport vocabulary in either failure text. "Account for real cases" ([job 140838600386](https://github.com/openJiuwen-ai/sciencediscovery/actions/runs/46080401663/job/140838600386)) reports the same single failure: `Planned 22; executed 22; passed 21; provider faults 0.`

**The search finished; only the delivery assertion failed.** Before line 172 the case already asserts, and passes:

- line 146: `expect(["succeeded", "budget_exhausted"]).toContain(search.status)` — the search reached a terminal state;
- line 151: the `search_finished` event agrees with the persisted run;
- line 157: `expect(expectedHash).toBeTruthy()` — the finished event names a result node (its `bestNodeIndex`) and a code hash.

So this is neither "the evolve search did not run" nor "the delivered code was queried wrongly".

**Why no artifact exists when the search finished.** Publication is a deliberately narrow path:

- `services/api/src/evolution/orchestrator.ts:888-905` (`finish`): the winner is handed to the publisher only when `status === "succeeded" && bestNodeIndex !== undefined`. A `budget_exhausted` run records its state and publishes nothing.
- `services/api/src/evolution/orchestrator.ts:910-925` (`publishWinner`): returns without publishing when no `expanded` event carries `bestNodeIndex`. That is the node-0 / seed case: no candidate beat the starting point, so there is no result to save. Intended, and pinned by the UT "nothing is published when the seed won" (`orchestrator.test.ts:928`).
- `services/api/src/bootstrap/platform.ts:346-348` (`publishResult`): returns silently when the winner source cannot be read.

Therefore one of exactly two outcomes produced this failure, and the case's own earlier assertions already confine it to them:

1. `search.status === "budget_exhausted"` — the control plane tripped the token/cost gate (`tripBudget`), the sidecar stopped, no artifact is published; or
2. `search.status === "succeeded"` with `bestNodeIndex === 0` — the seed stayed best, no artifact is published.

The spec accepts both statuses at line 146 and then still requires an artifact at line 172, so for either outcome the assertion can never pass. Its comment at line 163, "If the seed stayed best, its original artifact is also valid delivery", is not achievable either: the seed version is created only inside `publishResult` (`platform.ts:354`), which is never called on that path. The documented product behavior agrees with the code, not with the spec: `docs/zh/domains/evolve-a-solution.md:88` says only that *a search with an improvement* saves the starting point and the best code as two versions of the same result artifact.

**Why a race or a wrong query path is ruled out.** `finish` awaits `publishWinner` before the terminal record is published to subscribers, and the case looks for the artifact only after it has seen the terminal status (its own loop polls every 10 s) and re-read the `search_finished` event, then polls for another 30 s. If publication had happened, it would already be committed when the poll starts. The routes the case uses (`GET /api/sessions/:id/artifacts`, `.../artifacts/:id/versions`, `.../artifact-versions/:id/content`) are the ones the product exposes, and the same code passed this case the previous night.

**Impact.**

- Nightly/L5 goes red for a search that legitimately completed with nothing to deliver — the case's own criterion ("search finished normally") is met while its delivery criterion is unreachable.
- The failure costs two ~19 minute paid runs (attempt + retry) and cannot be told apart from a real delivery bug by reading the log.
- Every skip path above is silent: no `apiLog` line records "finished, but nothing published", so the only symptom is a 30 s predicate timeout with `Received: undefined`.
- A user who lets an evolve search run out of budget sees a finished search with no result artifact and no explanation of why.

**Suggested fix.**

1. *Use case (recommended, smallest change).* Make the delivery assertion follow the outcome the search actually had: require the artifact, its version hash and its content only when `search.status === "succeeded" && bestIndex > 0`; otherwise assert the terminal state and keep recording the scorecard, with a comment naming the product rule (nothing to deliver when the seed won or the search stopped on budget). The hash-selection and content assertions stay unchanged for an improving search.
2. *Product (a maintainer decision, not a test fix).* Publish the best-scoring candidate also on `budget_exhausted`, because the sidecar already gave that candidate its held-out score — only if the intended meaning is "a budget stop still delivers its best result". This changes the documented behavior above and the pinned UT.

Either way, add one `apiLog.info` when publication is skipped (`bestNodeIndex === 0`, `status === "budget_exhausted"`, or a candidate-read miss) so the next occurrence names its reason instead of a bare predicate timeout.

### Detailed Environment Information Description

- GitHub Actions `ubuntu-26.04` runner, workflow **Nightly** (`workflow_dispatch`), `profile: daily`, `CI_E2E_BACKEND=jiuwenswarm`, `E2E_LLM_MODEL=deepseek-flash` over an OpenAI-compatible endpoint, bubblewrap sandbox, `E2E_PUCT_LLM_EVALUATION=1`; `E2E_EVOLVE_RUN_TIMEOUT_MS` unset, so the case's 7 200 000 ms budget applies (not the cause: both attempts ended after ~19 min).
- Per-shard stack: adapter on 4410 in front of the Node API on 4510, runner on 4411, memory-graph, evolve sidecar. The retry ran in `.ci-retry/real-standard-retry` with its own data dir and its own stack.
